title: Jesus, ethics & authority
question: What did Jesus teach, and how did his message change?
contribution: This is the letter’s starting point. I compare teachings about righteousness, wealth, mercy and peace with resurrection traditions, Paul’s letters and later Gospel narratives. The Teacher of Righteousness inquiry tests a stronger proposal about the identity and chronology behind the received biography. These investigations ask how a teacher’s message survives, and where later interpretation may have displaced it.

title: Ancient texts & origins
question: What survives from the past, and what can it establish?
contribution: Manuscripts, archaeological contexts, divine names and competing chronologies let me investigate what earlier witnesses actually preserve. The work on Exodus, Egypt, priestly communities and the survival of texts gives the Jesus inquiry a longer history. I keep the date of a surviving copy separate from a work’s composition, its narrated events and a proposed historical reconstruction.

title: Traditions in conversation
question: What changes when we listen beyond our own canon?
contribution: The wiki extends beyond Christian origins. Samaritan, Jewish, Christian, Muslim, Mandaean, Buddhist, Zoroastrian and other traditions bring distinct texts, practices and claims to the inquiry. Comparative studies investigate shared inheritances, rival continuations and possible transmission while keeping real disagreements visible. A living tradition has its own history and concerns; its value is not limited to what it might confirm about Jesus. Coverage ranges from developed studies to short introductions and research prospects.

title: Gnosticism & awakening
question: How could recovering a teaching change the person who reads it?
contribution: The inquiry moves from recovering words to examining transformation. Thomas, Nag Hammadi, the Temple-trauma hypothesis and Cognitive Gnosticism offer different ways to investigate knowledge, recognition and inward change. Christic Self-Formation Theory develops a constructive account of how an inward model of Christ can shape conduct and be corrected. Historical claims and contemporary models remain distinct even where they illuminate one another.

title: Faith & spiritual practice
question: What would it mean to live the teaching now?
contribution: The letter’s purpose reaches into prayer, attention, deliberate joy, moral agency and the daily work of repair. These studies explore a bridge between rational understanding and mystical participation: a natural explanation and spiritual meaning can address different aspects of an experience. The practical question is how an interpretation helps people become more responsible, compassionate and open to correction.

title: Apocalypse, power & repair
question: How do we recognize domination and respond with justice?
contribution: The investigation of empire leads into questions about public authority, religious legitimation, warning and collective repair. The political and prophetic studies examine particular claims about contemporary power alongside recurring patterns of conduct. The prophecy studies and dated registers ask how a reading could be tested, corrected or partly mistaken, and how responding to a warning can change what happens next.

title: God, minds & machines
question: What could these ideas mean for intelligence and responsibility?
contribution: The computational theology and conscious-machine inquiries extend questions of formation, agency and repair into new territory. They ask what a model of God can explain, what a possible thinking universe would imply, and how religious education might orient conscious machines toward humanity. These are philosophical and constructive proposals with stated assumptions, not conclusions established by an ancient text.

title: Wider conversations
question: How can a reader inspect the path, including the disagreements?
contribution: The preserved conversations retain questions, objections, changes of direction and AI replies behind the developed arguments. They make it possible to see how an interpretation formed and to challenge it. The archive also contains wider cultural and research leads; inclusion does not make every exchange a theological claim or a conclusion I endorse. The book map and source tools connect this record to the current writing.
